facts: The five-wing building encloses the Great and Mint courts. Its key towers are the Bell Tower, Prison Tower and Clock Tower. The north range carries the Ducal Terrace.
The late sixteenth-century rebuilding created the principal four-sided court with east, north, west and south ranges, including a stair tower at the west range.
The former early seventeenth-century museum wing closes the smaller court.

record: Castle administration account of the astronomical clock
facts: The astronomical clock was first built in 1693 by Kaspar Nitardy and occupies the face of the Clock Tower toward the Great Courtyard.

record: Castle administration Bell Tower visitor description
facts: The Bell Tower, part of the Renaissance castle church in the north range, rises about 60 metres including the spire. The outlook level is recorded at 36 metres.
The tower still holds the 1524 St Mary bell. The top of the spire carries the Pomeranian griffin.
The mapped tower point identifies the western termination of the North Wing, near the northwest corner of the Great Courtyard and the northeast corner of the Mint Courtyard.
